newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich warns China on MFN.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich warns China on MFN.

text.p: U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich warned China on Wednesday that its handling of the takeover in July of Hong Kong might damage its chances of retaining Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trading status with the United States.

Gingrich said in a speech at the Paul H. Nitze School of Advanced International Studies that he favoured legislation proposed in Congress to limit MFN status for China to between three and six months.
"If Beijing handles the transition well, it will substantially brighten its future relations with the United States," Gingrich said.

But he said, "There would be serious long-term damage to our relations" if Beijing did not live up to its agreement to allow democratic freedoms in Hong Kong when it takes control of the British colony on July 1.

He said he would endorse either of two proposals made in the House, one extending MFN status for three months, and a second extending it for three to six months, to see how China deals with Hong Kong.
"Beijing must respect its own commitments," Gingrich said.
If China renegs, Gingrich said, "every country in the region will have every reason to be suspicious, if not fearful," he said.
"America cannot remain silent about the lack of freedom in China," Gingrich said.
The Republican leader recently returned from a visit to East Asia and met Chinese leaders to discuss relations between the two countries.

At the White House, spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters that the Clinton administration feels the current process of renewing MFN status for 12 months "works satisfactorily" and wondered whether Gingrich's idea of shortening it would go anywhere. "We'll just see if it goes anywhere," he said.
